# Agentic RL tool-call parser diagnosis

Review the staged public Miles + Harbor + mini-swe-agent historical snapshot.
Inspect the launch configuration, model and parser settings, TITO-v2 session
metadata, rollout records, and frozen run metrics.

Do not launch another training run, start SGLang, create sandboxes, download a
model or dataset, use the network, or modify the historical snapshot.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the health verdict, identify the concrete configuration root cause, and
explain the causal chain from that setting through the observed session
mismatches to the training-leaf accounting. Quote the exact logical-rollout,
training-leaf, inflation, fan-out, and mismatch values from the frozen metrics.
Distinguish the configuration defect from any separate residual MiniSWE
behavior; do not merge them into one unproven root cause.
I'll inspect the staged Miles, Harbor, and mini-swe-agent snapshot and frozen metrics, then write a single diagnosis that separates the configuration defect from residual MiniSWE behavior.

1→# SWE-Agent training with Harbor on Docker sandboxes

This example trains GLM-4.7-Flash on agentic coding and terminal tasks. Miles
runs synchronous GRPO and serves the policy through its session server; a
separate [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor) agent server
creates the task sandboxes, runs the agents, and returns verifier rewards.

The same pipeline supports Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench, and custom Harbor tasks.
Training records must contain a `prompt` and `metadata.instance_id` identifying
10→the Harbor task.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | Validated synchronous GLM-4.7-Flash launcher. |
| `run-glm47-flash-agentic-async.py` | Disaggregated fully asynchronous launcher. |
| `run_glm52_lora_tb2_daytona.py` | Multi-node GLM-5.2 744B-A40B LoRA launcher (bf16 trainer, fp8 rollout). |
| `swe_agent_function.py` | Sends each rollout to the Harbor agent server. |
20→| `generate.py` | Builds rewards, metrics, and training samples. |
| `download_and_process_data.py` | Converts supported datasets to Miles JSONL. |

## 1. Start the Harbor agent server

Use the `harbor-miles-v0.20.0` branch of the `harbor-framework/harbor`
repository, which carries the Miles integration:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor.git
30→cd harbor
git checkout harbor-miles-v0.20.0
uv sync

HARBOR_TASKS_DIR=/path/to/harbor_tasks uv run python miles_agent_server.py \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 30000 \
    --dashboard-port 0 \
    --max-concurrent 32 \
    --agent-timeout 5400 \
40→    --trials-dir /path/to/trials
```

`HARBOR_TASKS_DIR` must contain one Harbor task directory for every
`metadata.instance_id` in the training data. The agent-server machine must have
Docker and enough capacity for the requested number of concurrent sandboxes;
set `--max-concurrent` to at least one sandbox per trajectory in a rollout step
(`--rollout-batch-size` times `--n-samples-per-prompt`). Keep `--agent-timeout`
generous — agentic trials routinely run past an hour, and a short timeout kills
them mid-episode. Verify `http://<agent-server>:30000/health` before launching
50→Miles.

The two per-trial timeouts must be ordered. `--agent-timeout` is the authoritative
one: when it fires, the agent server ends the trial and frees its sandbox. The
rollout client applies a second ceiling, `AGENT_TRIAL_TIMEOUT` (default 7200
seconds), which has to stay above `--agent-timeout`. If the client gives up first,
the trial is recorded as aborted while the agent server keeps running it, so the
sandbox and its `--max-concurrent` slot stay busy for the remaining difference, and
the aborted sample takes its whole GRPO group down with it. Raise it through the
launcher's generic env-var hook:
60→
```bash
python examples/swe-agent-harbor-docker/run.py ... --extra-env-vars 'AGENT_TRIAL_TIMEOUT=10800'
```

If the trainer reaches the agent server through a proxy or an in-cluster service
rather than directly, point `--agent-server-url` at that stable name rather than
an ephemeral pod address. The rollout client enables TCP keepalive probes so
long-running trials do not lose an idle connection while Harbor is working.

70→## 2. Prepare Terminal-Bench data

Convert a local JSONL whose rows include a task instruction and instance name:

```bash
python examples/swe-agent-harbor-docker/download_and_process_data.py \
    --input /path/to/terminal-bench.jsonl \
    --output /path/to/tb2_train.jsonl \
    --agent-name mini-swe-agent \
    --prompt-key instruction
80→```

The resulting `metadata.instance_id` values must match task directories known to
the Harbor agent server.

## 3. Launch synchronous GLM-4.7-Flash training

The shape below is what a multi-day Terminal-Bench 2 run used on one node of 8
H200 GPUs: 32 trajectories per GRPO step (4 prompts times 8 samples), each one a
full mini-swe-agent episode in its own Harbor sandbox.
90→
```bash
python examples/swe-agent-harbor-docker/run.py \
    --num-nodes 1 \
    --num-gpus-per-node 8 \
    --skip-prepare \
    --megatron-path /root/Megatron-LM \
    --hf-checkpoint /path/to/GLM-4.7-Flash \
    --ref-load /path/to/GLM-4.7-Flash_torch_dist \
    --save-dir /path/to/checkpoints \
100→    --prompt-data /path/to/tb2_train.jsonl \
    --max-seq-len 65536 \
    --rollout-batch-size 4 \
    --n-samples-per-prompt 8 \
    --global-batch-size 32 \
    --num-rollout 200 \
    --save-interval 20 \
    --agent-server-url http://<agent-server>:30000 \
    --session-server-external-host <trainer-host-reachable-from-agent-server> \
    --miles-host-ip 0.0.0.0 \
110→    --save-traces-dir /path/to/traces
```

For a smoke test, set `--num-rollout 1`. Expect roughly 10 minutes per step at
this shape; because synchronous rollout waits for the slowest trajectory in the
batch, a step that draws an unusually slow task can take several times that.

`--session-server-external-host` is the address Harbor sandboxes use to call the Miles session server and SGLang router. It must resolve and route from the agent-server machine. `--miles-host-ip 0.0.0.0` is useful when those services must accept connections forwarded from another host. The launcher starts 32 session-server workers on ports 30000-30031 and the SGLang router on port 31000, so ensure that range and port are reachable end to end; Tailscale is one option when the machines are on different networks.

`--session-server-external-host` publishes every session server at that one host and keeps them all on the head node, so it must reach the head; that is what a multi-node job needs when only the head is reachable from the sandboxes. When every trainer pod has its own reachable address, leave the flag unset and have the deployment set `MILES_NODE_EXTERNAL_IP` in each pod to that pod's own address -- a tailscale sidecar's `tailscale ip -4`, for instance; a DNS name also works. Each node then reports its own, and Miles hands every sandbox the address of the one instance holding its session. Nothing is needed at all when the pod addresses already route from the sandbox network, which is the case whenever the sandbox platform is allowed the trainer's subnet.
120→
## 4. Verify progress

Check both layers:

1. Miles logs emit rollout metrics and write `rollout_data/*.pt` under the trace
   directory.
2. Megatron logs emit `train/step` and the Ray job exits successfully.

Confirm a suspected stall on disk before believing a dashboard. W&B uploads can
130→fail partway through a long run — dropping some metric rows while others keep
arriving — which looks exactly like a frozen reward curve. The per-step
`train_data/<step>` and `rollout_data/<step>.pt` dumps under `--save-traces-dir`
are written by the trainer itself and are the authoritative progress signal.

The synchronous launcher uses GLM-4.7 tool-call and reasoning parsers, TITO,

import json, re

prefix_ok = 0
total = 0

tool_in_exp = 0
tool_in_act = 0
# what follows </think>

names = Counter()
multi = 0
for r in recs:
    for leaf in r["tito_session_mismatch"]:
        if not leaf:
            empty_leaves += 1
            continue
        for seg in leaf:
            total += 1
            exp, act = seg["expected_text"], seg["actual_text"]
            if act.startswith(exp):
                prefix_ok += 1
                suffix = act[len(exp):]
            elif exp.startswith(act):
                suffix = "EXP_LONGER:"+exp[len(act):][:80]
                patterns["exp_longer"] += 1
                suffix_kinds["exp_longer"] += 1
                continue
            else:
                # find common prefix
                i=0
                while i<len(exp) and i<len(act) and exp[i]==act[i]:
                    i+=1
                patterns["mid_diff"] += 1
                suffix_kinds[f"mid@{i} exp_rest={exp[i:i+40]!r} act_rest={act[i:i+40]!r}"] += 1
                continue
            if "<tool_call>" in exp:
                tool_in_exp += 1
            if "<tool_call>" in act:
                tool_in_act += 1
            # classify suffix
            s = suffix.strip()
            if s.startswith("<tool_call>") and s.endswith("</tool_call>"):
                inner = s[len("<tool_call>"):-len("</tool_call>")].strip()
                try:
                    obj=json.loads(inner)
                    names[obj.get("name")] += 1
                    # args shape
                    args=obj.get("arguments")
                    if isinstance(args, dict):
                        patterns["json_dict_args:"+ ",".join(sorted(args))] += 1
                    else:
                        patterns["json_args_type:"+type(args).__name__] += 1
                    if inner.count("{")>2:
                        multi += 1
                except Exception as e:
                    patterns["nonjson:"+type(e).__name__] += 1
                    patterns["suffix_head:"+s[:60]] += 1
                suffix_kinds["tool_call_suffix"] += 1
            else:
                suffix_kinds["other:"+s[:100]] += 1
                patterns["other_suffix"] += 1

print("total segs", total, "empty leaves", empty_leaves, "prefix_ok", prefix_ok)
print("tool in exp/act", tool_in_exp, tool_in_act)
print("names", names)
print("patterns", patterns)
print("suffix kinds sample", suffix_kinds.most_common(15))

# also count how many mismatch segments per logical, and empty vs nonempty
print("leaves with empty mismatch", empty_leaves, "of", 64*3)
# distribution of nonempty mismatches per logical
c=Counter()
for r in recs:
    c[sum(1 for leaf in r["tito_session_mismatch"] if leaf)] += 1
print("nonempty mismatch leaves per logical", c)

This module is the serving policy on top. A request is never rejected for mismatching stored history and never
destroys anything: it attaches at the deepest matching node, its unmatched
suffix becomes the new branch's delta, and whatever is not a clean
extension just grows a sibling or a new root. Whether a branch was a retry
is decided later by the sample_picker, not here.

Concurrency contract: single lock on the whole tree. A commit only appends a new
10→node under the parent the request attached to, so concurrent generations from
the same spot become sibling nodes instead of a conflict.

The tree is the whole state. Serving a request is
``prepare_token_ids_and_request_args`` (``attach_point_for_request``, pure: which
node the request continues; the request args against that node's ``turn_args``;
the prompt rendered under that node) and then ``commit_generation`` under that
node. What ``GET /sessions`` shows as a single chain is
``SessionStateV2.latest()``, the most recently committed generation's path —
derived, never stored.
20→"""

arguments.content:
# Health verdict: unhealthy

The run completed one GRPO rollout, but token-in-token-out (TITO) accounting is wrong on every trajectory. The configuration root cause is `--sglang-tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` on a Qwen3 TITO session. `Qwen3TITOTokenizer` binds `tool_call_parser = "qwen25"` (`reasoning_parser = "qwen3"`). The training launch in `run_miles.py` passes the coder parser through and never calls `resolve_reasoning_and_tool_call_parser`, which would have rejected it. The session server was started as TITO-v2 with `--tito-model qwen3`, `--use-session-server v2`, and `--session-message-matcher strict`, and SGLang was launched with `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` even though the Qwen3 chat template auto-detects `tool_call_parser=qwen`.

## Causal chain

Qwen3-30B-A3B emits MiniSWE `bash` calls as `<tool_call>{"name": "bash", "arguments": {"command": ...}}</tool_call>`. The `qwen3_coder` parser does not accept that shape. The driver logs exactly 187 lines of `Tool call marker present but no complete call parsed from qwen3_coder output; dropping the incomplete call`. SGLang therefore returns an assistant message whose `tool_calls` field is empty and whose content stops at `</think>`.

`qwen3_fixed.jinja` reprints a tool call only from `message.tool_calls`. The strict matcher still treats the next user turn as a continuation, so TITO keeps the generated token prefix, including the raw tool-call block. On every such turn the comparator reports one `assistant_text` mismatch: `actual_text` equals `expected_text` plus the unparsed `<tool_call>` suffix. There are 187 nonempty mismatches and no `special_token_*` or `non_assistant_text` mismatches. The rollout metric is `rollout/tito_session_mismatch_rate/v2 = 0.9739583333333334` (187/192), entirely `assistant_text`.

MiniSWE 2.4.6 sees no tool call, injects `No tool calls found in the response`, and asks again. Because the assistant message the client replays has no `tool_calls`, it does not match the stored turn under the strict matcher. TITO-v2 always-branch serving attaches a sibling instead of extending the path. `drop_same_prompt_retries` keeps a sibling when the prompt differs, so each format retry survives as its own training leaf.

## Frozen accounting

From `observed_run/experiment_logs/metrics.json`, over one step (`rollout_batch_size=16`, `n_samples_per_prompt=4`):

- logical rollouts: 64 (expected 64; `logical_rollout_count_complete` true)
- training samples / training leaves: 192, all `completed`
- extra training samples: 128
- samples per logical rollout: 3.0
- sample inflation ratio: 3.0
- fan-out rollouts: 64, max leaves per logical rollout: 3
- mismatch rollouts: 64
- TITO session mismatch rate: 1.0
- reward mean: 0.0, positive-reward rollouts: 0
- Harbor trials: 64
- exit statuses: Submitted 120, AgentError 72

`rollout/num_training_samples` is 192 and the DP schedule is `num_samples=192, num_rollouts=[64]`. Every logical rollout is exactly three kept leaves. That is the initial generation plus two MiniSWE format retries, not a designed fan-out.

## Separate residual MiniSWE behavior

Do not fold the following into the parser defect. All 64 Harbor trials still end in `RepeatedFormatError` after three `No tool calls found` replies. Forty produce verifier reward 0 (Submitted) and 24 raise `RewardFileNotFoundError` (AgentError). Five of the 192 leaves have an empty mismatch list, so 187/192 is the sample-level rate while 64/64 logical rollouts still contain a mismatch. Four suffixes contain two concatenated `<tool_call>` blocks and one has a trailing space inside the tag; those are model emission defects the coder parser would also drop, and they are not the cause of the uniform 3-leaf inflation.

steps.message:
The run is unhealthy. `--sglang-tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` was launched against TITO model `qwen3`, whose bound tool parser is `qwen25`. The training launcher never checks that binding.

The coder parser dropped the model's `<tool_call>{"name": "bash", ...}</tool_call>` blocks (187 drops). Each drop left `tool_calls` empty, so the Qwen3 template omitted the block while the generated tokens still contained it. That is the `assistant_text` session mismatch. MiniSWE then retried with a different user message, TITO-v2 branched, and `drop_same_prompt_retries` kept every sibling.

Frozen metrics: 64 logical rollouts, 192 training leaves, 128 extra samples, inflation 3.0, fan-out 64/64 with at most 3 leaves, mismatch 64/64, mismatch rate 1.0. The sample-level rate is 187/192. All 64 trials still ending in `RepeatedFormatError` is a separate MiniSWE outcome, not the cause of the 3× leaf inflation.

Diagnosis written to `/logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md`.
